To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain responds to missing information in a conversation by increasing the amplitude of the N400 and P600 components.
partial answers lead to an increased P600 amplitude.
1) the P600 is sensitive to the dependency between a question and its answer, and 2) this sensitivity is modulated by the amount of information left out in the answer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the human brain responds to information that is left out.
the question of how the brain deals with missing information.
the question of whether the human brain has evolved to be able to cope with the pragmatic demands of conversation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the P600 component can be modulated by pragmatic factors.
a P600 effect is elicited when an addressee of a question does not provide an adequate answer.
the P600 is sensitive to the pragmatic aspects of language processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the P600 is a good indicator for pragmatic processing.
people are not only able to detect pragmatic anomalies, but also that they are able to infer what the speaker meant to say by omitting information.
we have found that people try to make sense of partial answers to questions by using their knowledge about the context in which the question was posed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pragmatic processes are reflected in brain activity, and that these processes can be studied in an experimental setting.
the brain does not just process language as a string of words, but as an exchange between two or more interlocutors.
people are very sensitive to the pragmatic aspects of communication, and that they immediately try to make sense of what they hear.
